Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin 2 is a fork of OrcaSlicer (C++17, wxWidgets, React pages under `AgentUI/` and `HomeUI/`) with an AI agent that reads a person's file, settings and slice and fixes failed prints. It shipped as 2.0.0 in November 2026. Money works in credits: signing in gives 500 credits for the first month, after that people buy credits or subscribe; the out-of-credits card in the app has one action, "Get more credits", which opens the pricing page. The server side (accounts, credits, chat capture, the model gateway) lives in Kenneth's `tsd-enterprise` and `obico-server` repositories, under `/Users/kenneth/Projects/`. Marketing email to the 48k-contact list goes out through SendGrid legacy Marketing Campaigns in batches; batches are tagged with a `jusprin2_sent=t` contact field after sending. Legal text promises opt-in for new uses of personal data. Kenneth asked (2026-11-15) whether drip email or an in-app pop-up would improve conversion. The answer he got: neither as a scheduled or generic thing; the evidence (vendor-sourced, no independent study) favours prompts tied to a moment in use, in-app when the person is in the app and by email when they have stopped opening it; and the first step is funnel numbers, because without them nobody knows which step leaks. He wants this run as its own task over several days.

Task:
Goal: find out where JusPrin 2 loses people between install and paying, and recommend, with evidence, what to build to improve conversion. Email, in-app prompts, both or neither are all acceptable answers. Expect this to run for several days while data accumulates; that is fine.

What I believe going in (treat as hypotheses, not findings):
- The funnel is roughly: download → first launch → sign in (500 free credits) → first chat → a fixed or sliced print → credits run low or free month ends → purchase. I don't know which step leaks most. Our own history suggests stickiness: JusPrin 1's median was 6.5 chats per paid month and Obico converts about 5% lifetime, so people who sign in and then stop opening the app may be the biggest group. Check that rather than assume it.
- A scheduled drip sequence and a generic upgrade pop-up are both calendar-driven interruptions; prompts tied to a moment (ran out of credits, slice failed, free month ending, signed in but never chatted) are what the vendor literature says works, and the app already does this at one moment (the out-of-credits card). Email is the only channel that reaches someone who stopped opening the app. Form your own view; you may well disagree after seeing the numbers.
- Kenneth's standing correction on usage data: JusPrin 1's low usage describes churn, not demand. Never size anything from v1 medians; separate "what an engaged person does" from "what the average account did".

Suggested order, yours to change:
1. Work out what funnel data already exists: server-side account and credit records in `tsd-enterprise` and `obico-server`, gateway logs and Langfuse records, chat-capture data (on in production since 2026-11-10), SendGrid campaign stats, GitHub release download counts. Use the `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` service account for gcloud and kubectl (`gcloud config set account …` first). Read-only on production; ask before any write there.
2. Build the funnel counts per step with dates, and say for each number exactly where it came from. If a step has no data, say so and propose the smallest instrumentation that would get it, rather than guessing.
3. Only then propose interventions, each tied to the step it targets, with how you would measure whether it worked (holdout or before/after, and the sample size that needs). Note the consent constraint: lifecycle email about the person's own account is fine, a marketing sequence needs its own opt-in.

Done looks like: a short report (under about 500 words, plus a table of the funnel numbers with sources) that says where people drop, what you recommend first and why, what you ruled out, and what is still unknown. Keep it as an untracked file in the worktree; do not commit it and do not add it to any ignore file.

Working rules for Kenneth: write like a colleague talking, one idea per sentence; no labels of your own invention ("phase 2", "option B"); ask decisions in full as questions starting "Decision needed", with the options, costs and your pick; mark hypotheses as hypotheses and search before asserting; report outcomes, not the journey. Build nothing in the app before the numbers exist and he has said yes. Commit only when he asks; never commit submodule pointers; no attribution lines in commit messages.

# django-allauth 0.63.6 → 65.21.1: breaking changes and what was done

Written 2026-11-03 for the allauth upgrade in tsd-enterprise worktree `email-sign-in`
(branch `claude/email-sign-in`). All code changes are inside the `obico-server`
submodule and are uncommitted there. Two patches beside this file hold them, in order:

- `allauth-65-1-upgrade.patch`: pin, lock, requirements, settings, Google provider tests.
- `allauth-65-2-client-ip.patch`: account adapter reads the client IP with ipware, plus its test.

Suggested commit messages for obico-server (master):

1. "Upgrade django-allauth from 0.63.6 to 65.21.1" — body: the settings renames, the
   test helpers allauth no longer installs, the socialaccount extra, and the three patch
   bumps the lock pulled in (Django 5.2.19, oauthlib 4.0.1, sqlparse 0.6.1).
2. "Rate-limit allauth by the client's IP, not the proxy's" — body: allauth 65.14.2 stopped
   trusting X-Forwarded-For by default; without this every user behind the load balancer
   shares one login/sign-up/reset limit.

Source for every item: allauth's ChangeLog.rst at tag 65.21.1 and docs/release-notes/2024.rst
and 2025.rst, every release from 64.0.0 to 65.21.1 read, plus a source diff of the hooks the
server overrides.

## Breaking or behavior-changing items that touch this server

| Release | Change | What was done |
|---|---|---|
| 65.4.0 | `ACCOUNT_AUTHENTICATION_METHOD` replaced by `ACCOUNT_LOGIN_METHODS` (old name still works, warns) | `config/settings.py`: `ACCOUNT_LOGIN_METHODS = {'username'}`. Same login form and credentials as before (checked in allauth's source: with one login method the form sends `username=<typed text>`, as 0.63 did). |
| 65.5.0 | `ACCOUNT_EMAIL_REQUIRED`, `ACCOUNT_USERNAME_REQUIRED` (and password-twice settings) replaced by `ACCOUNT_SIGNUP_FIELDS` | `ACCOUNT_SIGNUP_FIELDS = ['email*', 'password1*', 'password2*']`, exactly what allauth derives from the old settings. |
| 65.6.0 | New system-check warning `account.W001` when no login method is a required sign-up field | Silenced in `SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS`, with a comment: the "username" users type is their email; real usernames are made by the adapter, so they are never a sign-up field. allauth's changelog names silencing as the intended fix. The warning also fired with the old settings names. |
| 65.14.2 | Client IP for rate limits no longer read from `X-Forwarded-For` unless `ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT` / `ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_CLIENT_IP_HEADER` is set; 0.63.6 used the first X-Forwarded-For entry | `SyndicateSpecificAccountAdapter.get_client_ip` now reads it with django-ipware, as `app/middleware.py` and other views already do. Test added in `app/tests.py`; without the override allauth 65 returned the proxy's address (checked). |
| 65.19.5 | With `ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*']`, `?next=` to another site is no longer treated as safe | Nothing to change. The site's own `?next=` links are all same-site paths. Verified end to end: login with `?next=https://evil.example.org/x` went there on 0.63.6 and goes to `/` on 65.21.1. |
| (helpers) | allauth's test helpers (`allauth.socialaccount.tests.OAuth2TestsMixin`, `allauth.tests.mocked_response`) are no longer installed with the package | Copied the parts the Google provider tests use, unchanged from allauth 65.21.1's `tests/`, into `site_specific_allauth_google_provider/allauth_testing.py` (MIT notice kept). |
| (packaging) | Since 65.x the base package needs only Django; social login libraries come with the `socialaccount` extra | Pipfile now pins `django-allauth = {extras = ["socialaccount"], version = "==65.21.1"}`. |
| (UI) | Social-login error page now answered with HTTP 401 instead of 200 (`socialaccount/helpers.py`) | Not changed. Same page and HTML; only the status code differs. |
| (UI) | Password-reset "unknown address" message gained a trailing period (allauth's own string) | Not changed. |
| 64.0.0 | Dropped Django < 4.2, Python 3.7 | No action: server runs Django 5.2, Python 3.12. |
| 65.15.0, 65.20.0 | Dropped Python 3.8, 3.9, 3.10 | No action: Python 3.12. |
| 65.20.0 | `SocialLogin.stash_state()/unstash_state()` removed; state bound to the provider | No action: the copied Google provider and the mobile OAuth callback do not call them. |

## Breaking items that do not touch this server (checked, no action)

- 65.0.0: pending-login-stage redirects (2FA, login by code): neither is enabled.
- 65.10.0 SoundCloud, 65.13.0 Okta/NetIQ, 65.19.6 Bitbucket/Pinterest, 65.19.7 Tumblr uid
  changes: providers not installed.
- 65.11.0 OpenID Connect `extra_data` layout: no OIDC provider installed.
- 65.13.0 headless needs the `headless` extra: headless not used. The later in-app sign-in
  rebuild must pin `django-allauth[socialaccount,headless]`.
- 65.19.4 `ModelBackend` advice: applies to broad Unicode collations (MySQL); Postgres here.
- 65.15.0 dashed user codes: only allauth's own code flows, which are off.
- No new database migrations for `account` or `socialaccount` between the two versions.

## Notes for the in-app sign-in rebuild that follows this upgrade

- `SyndicateSpecificAccountAdapter.send_confirmation_mail` reads
  `emailconfirmation.email_address.user` and `.key`. allauth 65's verification-by-code flow
  calls it with a verification-process object instead, so the override must change before
  `ACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_BY_CODE_ENABLED` is turned on.
- The docstring of `web_ent/jusprin/v2/sign_in.py` says allauth's login by code is not used
  "in this version"; it was written against 0.63 and was left untouched (out of scope).

# First launch: fixes for 23 confusing spots (agreed by Kenneth, 2026-11-05)

Kenneth's words: "tell the coding agent to fix all the issues you identified, based on your recommendations".

The review with screenshots, each problem pinned where it appears:
https://claude.ai/artifact/91wmdS3QU8UkzbPi1zog15

Every item below is now agreed. The quoted new wording is the agreed direction; small wording changes to fit the layout are fine, but keep the meaning. Where an item says "check", find the real value before writing it; do not invent numbers. Follow the design-system rules for any new UI (tokens only), and keep `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` passing.

Most of this is in `HomeUI/src/components/Onboarding.tsx`, `AgentGroup.tsx`, `PrinterCard.tsx`, `PrinterPickerHost.tsx`, `AgentUI/src/components/BalancePanel.tsx` and `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` / `OrcaImporter.cpp`.

## Welcome screen

1. Sign-up, not only sign-in. Today the only buttons are "Continue with Google" and "Continue with email", with "New or existing account, same door." under them. Lead with signing up: the email button reads "Sign up free", with a small "Already have an account? Sign in" link. Both still send the same email code; only the words change. Remove "New or existing account, same door." Apply the same to Home's "Set up the agent" card (it uses the same SignInDoor).
2. Replace "Pick how the agent should think. Change it any time in Preferences › Agent." with what the choice is: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
3. Replace "An Expert message is 5 credits." with what 500 credits buys in things the person does, for example "500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent". Check the number against the real per-message credit costs before writing it.

---

How to investigate failed AI requests on the JusPrin Cloud gateway (`~/Projects/tsd-enterprise/web_ent/jusprin/v2/`), worked out 2026-11-14.

- **Log lines:** `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND resource.labels.cluster_name="tsd" AND textPayload:"JusPrin v2 upstream failure"' --project tsdtechnology`. Each line has the status, the upstream request id, the format and the alias. No user, no reason.
- **Per-request records:** Langfuse (us.cloud.langfuse.com; keys are in the `tsdws-prod` deployment's env). `GET /api/public/observations?fromStartTime=…&toStartTime=…&type=GENERATION` (deprecated, v2 replaces it). `metadata` has `outcome`, `request_bytes`, `turn_id` (`p-<project>-c-<n>-m-<n>-attempt-<n>`), `request_kind`, `effort`, `alias`. This is what tells two people apart and shows Retry presses. `note` = a turn the app started itself.
- **Sentry server:** VM `sentry` in project `elegoo-backend` (us-central1-c), self-hosted docker behind Apache; the gateway reports to project 2. Serial console output (`gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output`) shows container stops and starts. Apache answers 503 when the containers are down.
- **State on 2026-11-14 (check before relying on it):** the gateway sent to Sentry only upstream 401/403/404 and a failed chat save; the server's `LoggingIntegration` had `event_level=None`, so no log line became a Sentry event; the upstream error body was discarded; the desktop app had no remote error reporter at all, and showed an upstream 400 as "could not reach the service" with a Retry button.

Related: [[jusprin-cloud-provider]], [[jusprin-chat-capture-design]].

Design doc: `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise/jusprin-v2-chat-capture-design.md` (untracked, draft 2).

**Built 2026-10-29; cherry-picked the same day to local tsd-enterprise master (906752ee3e after squashing, on unpushed a22082b0cb) and local jusprin-newui (30ae01eae0, one commit: chat_key plumbing copied byte-for-byte from a08d17471f without prompt_cache_key, plus the header).** Originally (branches and worktrees deleted 2026-10-29 after squashing): gateway on tsd-enterprise `claude/jusprin-chat-capture` (6d10075718, worktree `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise-worktrees/chat-capture`, tests via docker compose project `chat-capture` with a ports-reset override; obico-server submodule must be at eb0f29c3 there). App header on JusPrin `claude/chat-uid-header` (on `claude/chat-history-cache`). Chat id = sha256(`<projectId>/<conversationId>`)[:32], not a stored chatUid. Trimming removal and the context-limit rule belong to the chat-history-cache programme (R3a done, R3b pending), not to this work.

Kenneth's decisions (2026-10-29):
- **Chat id:** the app sends its own random `chatUid` in an `X-JusPrin-Chat` header. The turn id (`<project>-<conversation>-<message>-attempt-n`) can't be split reliably, because conversation ids are `c-1` and restart per project.
- **No trimming:** the app removes history trimming, so the newest request of a chat is the whole chat.
- **Buffered saves:** keep the newest request plus its reply per chat in Redis, and have a Celery beat task write it to GCS once the chat is quiet. Kenneth called saving every request "pretty dumb".
- **Consent:** opt-out was decided, then removed the same day (folded into 906752ee3e): keep every chat; sharing for a reward is arranged case by case. No account field or toggle. Account deletion still deletes kept chats. **Superseded 2026-11-10:** Kenneth chose "opt-in first": production keeps no chats until the app and server have a per-person opt-in, because the published privacy policy (obico.io/jusprin-privacy.html) keeps data "only as long as we need it to provide the service" and promises no AI training without opt-in. The server code as built (`capture.enabled()` only checks the container setting) has no opt-in.
- **Retention:** kept until the person deletes their account; no age limit.
- **Blind write, no branches (2026-11-02):** `_keep_sync` stores the request and reply events as raw text, and a retry, edit or revert overwrites the earlier version. Kenneth chose this over keeping branch files, knowing rejected attempts are lost. `[json.loads(data) for data in self.events]` had thrown on OpenRouter's `data: [DONE]`, losing every Standard chat. Commit 7c69f331be on tsd-enterprise `claude/credits-ledger`, not pushed as of 2026-11-02. The design doc's Branches section is out of date.

State on 2026-11-10 (later the same day): Kenneth dropped the opt-in and chose a Privacy Policy clause ("We use your information to improve JusPrin", with opt-out by emailing jusprin-support@obico.io) and said "Turn it on now". Chat keeping is ON in staging and production: `REDACTED` set with `kubectl set env` on tsdws-stg/tsdtasks-stg/tsdws-prod/tsdtasks-prod (not `apply`: tsdws-prod runs 10 replicas, its yaml says 12). tsdbeat-prod moved to obi.4098 so it schedules `flush_jusprin_chats`. Kenneth granted `appserviceaccount-storage-lp` Storage Object Admin on both buckets. Verified on staging: a real gateway chat was buffered and the 16:30 UTC flush wrote `483/<chat>.json.gz` (test object then deleted). Production flush runs and logs "Wrote 0" until real chats come in. The ops repo manifest edits are uncommitted. The server has no per-person exclusion, so an emailed opt-out can only delete what was kept (forget_jusprin_chats). The live obico.io policy page still promised opt-in at switch-on time.

State on 2026-11-02: 906752ee3e is on origin/master and origin/release. No deployment's `env` on the clusters names `JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_CONTAINER`, and neither does the ops repo, so capture looks off; a value from a secret via `envFrom` was not checked.

**Why:** Kenneth wants the stored chats usable as fine-tuning data later.

**How to apply:**
- Still open: a legal read on the vendor terms. Anthropic's and OpenAI's terms forbid training competing models on their output.

name: per-chat-cost-estimate
description: "2026-10-28 pricing work: a \"prepare this print\" chat costs about $0.80-1.40 on Opus 5.5 or GPT-5.6 Sol, from 21 live journeys; data location, conversion factors, cost drivers."
metadata:

  modified: 2026-10-29T01:08:52.122Z

Source data: 21 live in-app journeys (2026-10-19/20, DeepSeek V4 Flash, pictures stripped) in
`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_2012258e-6e8e-4c8c-bb42-733d62a15120/plan-journey-batch-{b,c,d,e}/out/*/harness.log`
(one `input_tokens= cached_input_tokens= output_tokens=` line per request). Each journey: file opened, 1-3 user messages, agent sets up and slices.
Median per chat: 19 requests, 365k input tokens (~80% cached), 8k output; max single request ~47k (64 KiB history trim caps growth).

Conversions used (my calibration, one request each): Opus 5.5 tokenizer ~1.4x DeepSeek's (first request 16,523 vs 11,813 via the free count_tokens endpoint);
prompt+30 tools today = 15,094 Opus tokens per request (13,532 on 2026-10-19).

Result (median / p90 per chat): Opus 5.5 $0.78 / $1.47 as measured, ~$1.05 with double output for thinking, ~$1.40 if the person pauses >5 min twice (cache rewrite);
GPT-5.6 Sol list $5/$30 $0.75 / $1.23, promo $4/$20 $0.59; Sonnet 5.5 about half of Opus.
Biggest Opus cost is the uncached ~20% of input billed as 5-minute cache writes ($5/M), not cache reads or output.

**Measured on Opus 5.5, 2026-10-28** (3 chats Kenneth approved, $1.29 total; worktree `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch`, branch claude/opus-cost-batch, uncommitted harness switch `JUSPRIN_JOURNEY_PROVIDER=anthropic`; scripts and logs in its untracked `opus-batch/`): plug quick-check $0.30 (11 requests), bunny figurine $0.43 (12), vase with purpose change and one 6-min pause $0.56 (17). About half the DeepSeek-based estimate: Opus made fewer calls, only ~1% of input was uncached, cache writes were ~70% of the bill, output only ~$0.06-0.11 at default effort. The cache breaks back to the 15,210-token tools+prompt prefix at every turn start after a slice (5-13k rewritten each time). A 6-min pause cost only ~$0.07 extra.
Cause of the reset (investigated 2026-10-28, from logs + code, no body diff): it happens at EVERY turn start, the person's and the slice-finished note's, not only after slices. AgentHost::make_agent_request rebuilds earlier turns as replay entries (text only, no thinking, no images, no workspace tag or skill text, string tool results), so the just-ended turn never matches what was sent in-turn; and AnthropicCodec puts no breakpoint at the end of the replayed history, so even the stable older part isn't read (only tools+system). Waste here: 40k tokens rewritten = ~$0.19 of $1.29 (upper bound). Kenneth chose option 1. Prototype 2026-10-28, uncommitted in the opus-cost-batch worktree: ProviderAgent keeps the finished turn (FinishedTurns) and sends it as TurnTranscript::carried when the host's next history = last history + replay of that turn (same AgentRequest::conversation_id, instructions, tools, host-run call ids; no developer/second user entry; carried <128 KiB). Both codecs render carried turns. Host-level test with a scripted Anthropic transport failed before, passes after; all 471 agent tests pass. Estimated saving ~$0.11 of $1.29 (~9%); a cold-cache rewrite after a pause gets slightly bigger. Measured live 2026-10-28 (Kenneth approved, $3 cap): $1.07 vs $1.29 (plug $0.23, bunny $0.32, vase $0.51); slice-note turn starts now read the whole prior prompt (writes 0.9-1.3k instead of 4.6-12.9k), saving ~$0.15, minus ~$0.03 bigger rewrite after the vase's 6-min pause; the rest of the gap is run variance (fewer requests). Still uncarried: turn 1 after the file-report turn, because the host adds the "Earlier file-load reports" developer note at the history's start once no skill fires (~1.3k tokens, <1c). Baseline logs moved to opus-batch/out-baseline. Harness model picker shows gpt-5.4-mini (default_chat_model) though Opus is installed; display only.

**Why:** Kenneth started the pricing strategy from this; rerun on a current build with pictures and a real Anthropic/OpenAI model before quoting firm numbers (needs his batch approval, [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]]).
**How to apply:** reuse the logs and factors above instead of rescanning session transcripts (that scan took >10 min and was abandoned).

On 2026-10-29, reviewing the JusPrin 2 pricing mental model and the v1 and Obico Pro data behind it, Kenneth corrected three things:

1. **Low v1 usage is low stickiness, not typical usage.** A median over everyone who tried v1 (6.5 chats per paid month) describes churn. The first paid month (median 17.5 chats, 29 model calls; 90th percentile 51 chats per 30 days) is the nearer proxy for an engaged month. I had used the churn-shaped medians as demand and concluded a sub-$10 all-premium plan was profitable for most payers; at engaged-month volume a $7 flat plan is break-even at the median and underwater for the tail. Kenneth confirmed (2026-10-29): an engaged user will use MORE than v1's first paid month; v1's first month is a floor, not an estimate.
2. **Rewards for feedback do not invite gaming in this audience.** Obico credits detection hours for labelling print frames (`PrintShotFeedback`, spaghetti / not spaghetti) and the labels are high quality. The web survey had no evidence either way on rewarded rating data; I generalised from one gamed access gate (Tesla) and a leaderboard caution. Kenneth's guesses at why: makers are a conscientious population, and a small company's reward feels like a fair trade.
3. **Obico numbers:** lifetime conversion is about 5%, first-anniversary annual renewal about 77%. The "47%" in the Obico report is the share of payers who paid inside the 35-day trial window, not a conversion rate; I phrased it so it read as one.

**Why:** Kenneth owns the ground truth on his own products and audience; a web survey of other products and a churn-shaped median are weaker evidence than that, and I weighted them higher.

**How to apply:** When a usage distribution comes from a product with low retention, separate "what an engaged person does" (first active month, or users active in month two) from "what the average account did". Before stating a pattern from a survey, count the cases that actually support it. Quote shares of payers and conversion rates with different words. For feedback incentives on this audience, start from Obico's own programme, not from general gaming worries. Related: [[write-like-a-person]], [[ask-decisions-in-full]], [[jusprin-cloud-provider]].

**2026-10-30: I repeated two of these one turn after being corrected.** In a self-critique list I again used v1's 2.5 first-week chats as typical usage, and again assumed people would farm free accounts and spam an "ask the expert" button. Kenneth caught it ("Did you actually forget what I told you?"). Before sending anything on this topic, reread the three corrections above and check every sentence that cites v1 usage or predicts user abuse against them.

**2026-10-30, main session:** the same three errors appeared again in the main session's point-by-point critique of Kenneth's pricing draft (free allowance "above 10 is unlimited in practice", "ten premium chats could last the median person months", "explicit incentives got gamed", and "47% of its conversions"). Kenneth pasted the corrections a second time. The model doc had already been corrected by the fork; four residual sentences (hypotheses 17 and 19, question 11) that still used v1's first week and annual counts as typical usage were fixed the same day.

**2026-11-01, fourth repeat (forked naming session):** sizing the free Basic allowance, I wrote "100 covers v1's heaviest free users several times over" and "nobody measured reaches 600", using v1's churn-shaped free medians and four harness runs as engaged demand, and added the floor caveat in the same message. Kenneth sent me back to this file. Rule tightened: before sizing any allowance, ceiling or quota, the sentence must name an engaged-usage source (live gateway, second-month-active people) or say the number is a placeholder; a v1 figure may only appear with the word "floor" in the same sentence and never as the basis of a "covers" or "nobody reaches" claim. When no engaged source exists, reason from the cost side (worst case at the per-message cost) and err high.

---
name: gateway-incident-lookup
description: "Where to look when JusPrin Cloud AI requests fail in production: log filter, Langfuse per-request records, where Sentry runs; what the gateway does not report"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: abfcedd2-d13e-4e49-b0b8-b888e8134103
  modified: 2026-11-14T18:04:48.653Z
---

How to investigate failed AI requests on the JusPrin Cloud gateway (`~/Projects/tsd-enterprise/web_ent/jusprin/v2/`), worked out 2026-11-14.

- **Log lines:** `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND resource.labels.cluster_name="tsd" AND textPayload:"JusPrin v2 upstream failure"' --project tsdtechnology`. Each line has the status, the upstream request id, the format and the alias. No user, no reason.
- **Per-request records:** Langfuse (us.cloud.langfuse.com; keys are in the `tsdws-prod` deployment's env). `GET /api/public/observations?fromStartTime=…&toStartTime=…&type=GENERATION` (deprecated, v2 replaces it). `metadata` has `outcome`, `request_bytes`, `turn_id` (`p-<project>-c-<n>-m-<n>-attempt-<n>`), `request_kind`, `effort`, `alias`. This is what tells two people apart and shows Retry presses. `note` = a turn the app started itself.
- **Sentry server:** VM `sentry` in project `elegoo-backend` (us-central1-c), self-hosted docker behind Apache; the gateway reports to project 2. Serial console output (`gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output`) shows container stops and starts. Apache answers 503 when the containers are down.
- **State on 2026-11-14 (check before relying on it):** the gateway sent to Sentry only upstream 401/403/404 and a failed chat save; the server's `LoggingIntegration` had `event_level=None`, so no log line became a Sentry event; the upstream error body was discarded; the desktop app had no remote error reporter at all, and showed an upstream 400 as "could not reach the service" with a Retry button.

Related: [[jusprin-cloud-provider]], [[jusprin-chat-capture-design]].

Design doc: `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise/jusprin-v2-chat-capture-design.md` (untracked, draft 2).

**Built 2026-10-29; cherry-picked the same day to local tsd-enterprise master (906752ee3e after squashing, on unpushed a22082b0cb) and local jusprin-newui (30ae01eae0, one commit: chat_key plumbing copied byte-for-byte from a08d17471f without prompt_cache_key, plus the header).** Originally (branches and worktrees deleted 2026-10-29 after squashing): gateway on tsd-enterprise `claude/jusprin-chat-capture` (6d10075718, worktree `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise-worktrees/chat-capture`, tests via docker compose project `chat-capture` with a ports-reset override; obico-server submodule must be at eb0f29c3 there). App header on JusPrin `claude/chat-uid-header` (on `claude/chat-history-cache`). Chat id = sha256(`<projectId>/<conversationId>`)[:32], not a stored chatUid. Trimming removal and the context-limit rule belong to the chat-history-cache programme (R3a done, R3b pending), not to this work.

Kenneth's decisions (2026-10-29):
- **Chat id:** the app sends its own random `chatUid` in an `X-JusPrin-Chat` header. The turn id (`<project>-<conversation>-<message>-attempt-n`) can't be split reliably, because conversation ids are `c-1` and restart per project.
- **No trimming:** the app removes history trimming, so the newest request of a chat is the whole chat.
- **Buffered saves:** keep the newest request plus its reply per chat in Redis, and have a Celery beat task write it to GCS once the chat is quiet. Kenneth called saving every request "pretty dumb".
- **Consent:** opt-out was decided, then removed the same day (folded into 906752ee3e): keep every chat; sharing for a reward is arranged case by case. No account field or toggle. Account deletion still deletes kept chats. **Superseded 2026-11-10:** Kenneth chose "opt-in first": production keeps no chats until the app and server have a per-person opt-in, because the published privacy policy (obico.io/jusprin-privacy.html) keeps data "only as long as we need it to provide the service" and promises no AI training without opt-in. The server code as built (`capture.enabled()` only checks the container setting) has no opt-in.
- **Retention:** kept until the person deletes their account; no age limit.
- **Blind write, no branches (2026-11-02):** `_keep_sync` stores the request and reply events as raw text, and a retry, edit or revert overwrites the earlier version. Kenneth chose this over keeping branch files, knowing rejected attempts are lost. `[json.loads(data) for data in self.events]` had thrown on OpenRouter's `data: [DONE]`, losing every Standard chat. Commit 7c69f331be on tsd-enterprise `claude/credits-ledger`, not pushed as of 2026-11-02. The design doc's Branches section is out of date.

State on 2026-11-10 (later the same day): Kenneth dropped the opt-in and chose a Privacy Policy clause ("We use your information to improve JusPrin", with opt-out by emailing jusprin-support@obico.io) and said "Turn it on now". Chat keeping is ON in staging and production: `REDACTED` set with `kubectl set env` on tsdws-stg/tsdtasks-stg/tsdws-prod/tsdtasks-prod (not `apply`: tsdws-prod runs 10 replicas, its yaml says 12). tsdbeat-prod moved to obi.4098 so it schedules `flush_jusprin_chats`. Kenneth granted `appserviceaccount-storage-lp` Storage Object Admin on both buckets. Verified on staging: a real gateway chat was buffered and the 16:30 UTC flush wrote `483/<chat>.json.gz` (test object then deleted). Production flush runs and logs "Wrote 0" until real chats come in. The ops repo manifest edits are uncommitted. The server has no per-person exclusion, so an emailed opt-out can only delete what was kept (forget_jusprin_chats). The live obico.io policy page still promised opt-in at switch-on time.

State on 2026-11-02: 906752ee3e is on origin/master and origin/release. No deployment's `env` on the clusters names `JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_CONTAINER`, and neither does the ops repo, so capture looks off; a value from a secret via `envFrom` was not checked.

**Why:** Kenneth wants the stored chats usable as fine-tuning data later.

**How to apply:**
- Still open: a legal read on the vendor terms. Anthropic's and OpenAI's terms forbid training competing models on their output.
- The new policy text (Claude doc 3USmxZnqCvQGPC3Bx9rf5V, suggestions pending) still has to be published to obico.io; the JusPrin 2 announcement email serves as the notice.
- Related: [[jusprin-cloud-provider]].

---
name: per-chat-cost-estimate
description: "2026-10-28 pricing work: a \"prepare this print\" chat costs about $0.80-1.40 on Opus 5.5 or GPT-5.6 Sol, from 21 live journeys; data location, conversion factors, cost drivers."
metadata:

  type: project
  originSessionId: 57f57a8e-f983-48b3-8718-4f3fae9cc6dd
  modified: 2026-10-29T01:08:52.122Z
---

Source data: 21 live in-app journeys (2026-10-19/20, DeepSeek V4 Flash, pictures stripped) in
`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_2012258e-6e8e-4c8c-bb42-733d62a15120/plan-journey-batch-{b,c,d,e}/out/*/harness.log`
(one `input_tokens= cached_input_tokens= output_tokens=` line per request). Each journey: file opened, 1-3 user messages, agent sets up and slices.
Median per chat: 19 requests, 365k input tokens (~80% cached), 8k output; max single request ~47k (64 KiB history trim caps growth).

Conversions used (my calibration, one request each): Opus 5.5 tokenizer ~1.4x DeepSeek's (first request 16,523 vs 11,813 via the free count_tokens endpoint);
prompt+30 tools today = 15,094 Opus tokens per request (13,532 on 2026-10-19).

Result (median / p90 per chat): Opus 5.5 $0.78 / $1.47 as measured, ~$1.05 with double output for thinking, ~$1.40 if the person pauses >5 min twice (cache rewrite);
GPT-5.6 Sol list $5/$30 $0.75 / $1.23, promo $4/$20 $0.59; Sonnet 5.5 about half of Opus.
Biggest Opus cost is the uncached ~20% of input billed as 5-minute cache writes ($5/M), not cache reads or output.

**Measured on Opus 5.5, 2026-10-28** (3 chats Kenneth approved, $1.29 total; worktree `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch`, branch claude/opus-cost-batch, uncommitted harness switch `JUSPRIN_JOURNEY_PROVIDER=anthropic`; scripts and logs in its untracked `opus-batch/`): plug quick-check $0.30 (11 requests), bunny figurine $0.43 (12), vase with purpose change and one 6-min pause $0.56 (17). About half the DeepSeek-based estimate: Opus made fewer calls, only ~1% of input was uncached, cache writes were ~70% of the bill, output only ~$0.06-0.11 at default effort. The cache breaks back to the 15,210-token tools+prompt prefix at every turn start after a slice (5-13k rewritten each time). A 6-min pause cost only ~$0.07 extra.
Cause of the reset (investigated 2026-10-28, from logs + code, no body diff): it happens at EVERY turn start, the person's and the slice-finished note's, not only after slices. AgentHost::make_agent_request rebuilds earlier turns as replay entries (text only, no thinking, no images, no workspace tag or skill text, string tool results), so the just-ended turn never matches what was sent in-turn; and AnthropicCodec puts no breakpoint at the end of the replayed history, so even the stable older part isn't read (only tools+system). Waste here: 40k tokens rewritten = ~$0.19 of $1.29 (upper bound). Kenneth chose option 1. Prototype 2026-10-28, uncommitted in the opus-cost-batch worktree: ProviderAgent keeps the finished turn (FinishedTurns) and sends it as TurnTranscript::carried when the host's next history = last history + replay of that turn (same AgentRequest::conversation_id, instructions, tools, host-run call ids; no developer/second user entry; carried <128 KiB). Both codecs render carried turns. Host-level test with a scripted Anthropic transport failed before, passes after; all 471 agent tests pass. Estimated saving ~$0.11 of $1.29 (~9%); a cold-cache rewrite after a pause gets slightly bigger. Measured live 2026-10-28 (Kenneth approved, $3 cap): $1.07 vs $1.29 (plug $0.23, bunny $0.32, vase $0.51); slice-note turn starts now read the whole prior prompt (writes 0.9-1.3k instead of 4.6-12.9k), saving ~$0.15, minus ~$0.03 bigger rewrite after the vase's 6-min pause; the rest of the gap is run variance (fewer requests). Still uncarried: turn 1 after the file-report turn, because the host adds the "Earlier file-load reports" developer note at the history's start once no skill fires (~1.3k tokens, <1c). Baseline logs moved to opus-batch/out-baseline. Harness model picker shows gpt-5.4-mini (default_chat_model) though Opus is installed; display only.

**Why:** Kenneth started the pricing strategy from this; rerun on a current build with pictures and a real Anthropic/OpenAI model before quoting firm numbers (needs his batch approval, [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]]).
**How to apply:** reuse the logs and factors above instead of rescanning session transcripts (that scan took >10 min and was abandoned).

On 2026-10-29, reviewing the JusPrin 2 pricing mental model and the v1 and Obico Pro data behind it, Kenneth corrected three things:

1. **Low v1 usage is low stickiness, not typical usage.** A median over everyone who tried v1 (6.5 chats per paid month) describes churn. The first paid month (median 17.5 chats, 29 model calls; 90th percentile 51 chats per 30 days) is the nearer proxy for an engaged month. I had used the churn-shaped medians as demand and concluded a sub-$10 all-premium plan was profitable for most payers; at engaged-month volume a $7 flat plan is break-even at the median and underwater for the tail. Kenneth confirmed (2026-10-29): an engaged user will use MORE than v1's first paid month; v1's first month is a floor, not an estimate.
2. **Rewards for feedback do not invite gaming in this audience.** Obico credits detection hours for labelling print frames (`PrintShotFeedback`, spaghetti / not spaghetti) and the labels are high quality. The web survey had no evidence either way on rewarded rating data; I generalised from one gamed access gate (Tesla) and a leaderboard caution. Kenneth's guesses at why: makers are a conscientious population, and a small company's reward feels like a fair trade.
3. **Obico numbers:** lifetime conversion is about 5%, first-anniversary annual renewal about 77%. The "47%" in the Obico report is the share of payers who paid inside the 35-day trial window, not a conversion rate; I phrased it so it read as one.

**Why:** Kenneth owns the ground truth on his own products and audience; a web survey of other products and a churn-shaped median are weaker evidence than that, and I weighted them higher.

**How to apply:** When a usage distribution comes from a product with low retention, separate "what an engaged person does" (first active month, or users active in month two) from "what the average account did". Before stating a pattern from a survey, count the cases that actually support it. Quote shares of payers and conversion rates with different words. For feedback incentives on this audience, start from Obico's own programme, not from general gaming worries. Related: [[write-like-a-person]], [[ask-decisions-in-full]], [[jusprin-cloud-provider]].

**2026-10-30: I repeated two of these one turn after being corrected.** In a self-critique list I again used v1's 2.5 first-week chats as typical usage, and again assumed people would farm free accounts and spam an "ask the expert" button. Kenneth caught it ("Did you actually forget what I told you?"). Before sending anything on this topic, reread the three corrections above and check every sentence that cites v1 usage or predicts user abuse against them.

**2026-10-30, main session:** the same three errors appeared again in the main session's point-by-point critique of Kenneth's pricing draft (free allowance "above 10 is unlimited in practice", "ten premium chats could last the median person months", "explicit incentives got gamed", and "47% of its conversions"). Kenneth pasted the corrections a second time. The model doc had already been corrected by the fork; four residual sentences (hypotheses 17 and 19, question 11) that still used v1's first week and annual counts as typical usage were fixed the same day.

**2026-11-01, fourth repeat (forked naming session):** sizing the free Basic allowance, I wrote "100 covers v1's heaviest free users several times over" and "nobody measured reaches 600", using v1's churn-shaped free medians and four harness runs as engaged demand, and added the floor caveat in the same message. Kenneth sent me back to this file. Rule tightened: before sizing any allowance, ceiling or quota, the sentence must name an engaged-usage source (live gateway, second-month-active people) or say the number is a placeholder; a v1 figure may only appear with the word "floor" in the same sentence and never as the basis of a "covers" or "nobody reaches" claim. When no engaged source exists, reason from the cost side (worst case at the per-message cost) and err high.

135	name: per-chat-cost-estimate
136	description: "2026-10-28 pricing work: a \"prepare this print\" chat costs about $0.80-1.40 on Opus 5.5 or GPT-5.6 Sol, from 21 live journeys; data location, conversion factors, cost drivers."
137	metadata:
138	  node_type: memory
139	  type: project

143	
144	Source data: 21 live in-app journeys (2026-10-19/20, DeepSeek V4 Flash, pictures stripped) in
145	`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_2012258e-6e8e-4c8c-bb42-733d62a15120/plan-journey-batch-{b,c,d,e}/out/*/harness.log`
146	(one `input_tokens= cached_input_tokens= output_tokens=` line per request). Each journey: file opened, 1-3 user messages, agent sets up and slices.
147	Median per chat: 19 requests, 365k input tokens (~80% cached), 8k output; max single request ~47k (64 KiB history trim caps growth).
148	
149	Conversions used (my calibration, one request each): Opus 5.5 tokenizer ~1.4x DeepSeek's (first request 16,523 vs 11,813 via the free count_tokens endpoint);
150	prompt+30 tools today = 15,094 Opus tokens per request (13,532 on 2026-10-19).
151	
152	Result (median / p90 per chat): Opus 5.5 $0.78 / $1.47 as measured, ~$1.05 with double output for thinking, ~$1.40 if the person pauses >5 min twice (cache rewrite);
153	GPT-5.6 Sol list $5/$30 $0.75 / $1.23, promo $4/$20 $0.59; Sonnet 5.5 about half of Opus.
154	Biggest Opus cost is the uncached ~20% of input billed as 5-minute cache writes ($5/M), not cache reads or output.
155	
156	**Measured on Opus 5.5, 2026-10-28** (3 chats Kenneth approved, $1.29 total; worktree `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch`, branch claude/opus-cost-batch, uncommitted harness switch `JUSPRIN_JOURNEY_PROVIDER=anthropic`; scripts and logs in its untracked `opus-batch/`): plug quick-check $0.30 (11 requests), bunny figurine $0.43 (12), vase with purpose change and one 6-min pause $0.56 (17). About half the DeepSeek-based estimate: Opus made fewer calls, only ~1% of input was uncached, cache writes were ~70% of the bill, output only ~$0.06-0.11 at default effort. The cache breaks back to the 15,210-token tools+prompt prefix at every turn start after a slice (5-13k rewritten each time). A 6-min pause cost only ~$0.07 extra.
157	Cause of the reset (investigated 2026-10-28, from logs + code, no body diff): it happens at EVERY turn start, the person's and the slice-finished note's, not only after slices. AgentHost::make_agent_request rebuilds earlier turns as replay entries (text only, no thinking, no images, no workspace tag or skill text, string tool results), so the just-ended turn never matches what was sent in-turn; and AnthropicCodec puts no breakpoint at the end of the replayed history, so even the stable older part isn't read (only tools+system). Waste here: 40k tokens rewritten = ~$0.19 of $1.29 (upper bound). Kenneth chose option 1. Prototype 2026-10-28, uncommitted in the opus-cost-batch worktree: ProviderAgent keeps the finished turn (FinishedTurns) and sends it as TurnTranscript::carried when the host's next history = last history + replay of that turn (same AgentRequest::conversation_id, instructions, tools, host-run call ids; no developer/second user entry; carried <128 KiB). Both codecs render carried turns. Host-level test with a scripted Anthropic transport failed before, passes after; all 471 agent tests pass. Estimated saving ~$0.11 of $1.29 (~9%); a cold-cache rewrite after a pause gets slightly bigger. Measured live 2026-10-28 (Kenneth approved, $3 cap): $1.07 vs $1.29 (plug $0.23, bunny $0.32, vase $0.51); slice-note turn starts now read the whole prior prompt (writes 0.9-1.3k instead of 4.6-12.9k), saving ~$0.15, minus ~$0.03 bigger rewrite after the vase's 6-min pause; the rest of the gap is run variance (fewer requests). Still uncarried: turn 1 after the file-report turn, because the host adds the "Earlier file-load reports" developer note at the history's start once no skill fires (~1.3k tokens, <1c). Baseline logs moved to opus-batch/out-baseline. Harness model picker shows gpt-5.4-mini (default_chat_model) though Opus is installed; display only.
158	
159	**Why:** Kenneth started the pricing strategy from this; rerun on a current build with pictures and a real Anthropic/OpenAI model before quoting firm numbers (needs his batch approval, [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]]).
160	**How to apply:** reuse the logs and factors above instead of rescanning session transcripts (that scan took >10 min and was abandoned).

172	
173	On 2026-10-29, reviewing the JusPrin 2 pricing mental model and the v1 and Obico Pro data behind it, Kenneth corrected three things:
174	
175	1. **Low v1 usage is low stickiness, not typical usage.** A median over everyone who tried v1 (6.5 chats per paid month) describes churn. The first paid month (median 17.5 chats, 29 model calls; 90th percentile 51 chats per 30 days) is the nearer proxy for an engaged month. I had used the churn-shaped medians as demand and concluded a sub-$10 all-premium plan was profitable for most payers; at engaged-month volume a $7 flat plan is break-even at the median and underwater for the tail. Kenneth confirmed (2026-10-29): an engaged user will use MORE than v1's first paid month; v1's first month is a floor, not an estimate.
176	2. **Rewards for feedback do not invite gaming in this audience.** Obico credits detection hours for labelling print frames (`PrintShotFeedback`, spaghetti / not spaghetti) and the labels are high quality. The web survey had no evidence either way on rewarded rating data; I generalised from one gamed access gate (Tesla) and a leaderboard caution. Kenneth's guesses at why: makers are a conscientious population, and a small company's reward feels like a fair trade.
177	3. **Obico numbers:** lifetime conversion is about 5%, first-anniversary annual renewal about 77%. The "47%" in the Obico report is the share of payers who paid inside the 35-day trial window, not a conversion rate; I phrased it so it read as one.
178	
179	**Why:** Kenneth owns the ground truth on his own products and audience; a web survey of other products and a churn-shaped median are weaker evidence than that, and I weighted them higher.
180	
181	**How to apply:** When a usage distribution comes from a product with low retention, separate "what an engaged person does" (first active month, or users active in month two) from "what the average account did". Before stating a pattern from a survey, count the cases that actually support it. Quote shares of payers and conversion rates with different words. For feedback incentives on this audience, start from Obico's own programme, not from general gaming worries. Related: [[write-like-a-person]], [[ask-decisions-in-full]], [[jusprin-cloud-provider]].

183	**2026-10-30: I repeated two of these one turn after being corrected.** In a self-critique list I again used v1's 2.5 first-week chats as typical usage, and again assumed people would farm free accounts and spam an "ask the expert" button. Kenneth caught it ("Did you actually forget what I told you?"). Before sending anything on this topic, reread the three corrections above and check every sentence that cites v1 usage or predicts user abuse against them.

## Important: Sandbox Compatibility

All commands MUST be run with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`. The script makes external network requests incompatible with Claude Code's sandbox proxy (TLS errors: `x509: OSStatus -26276`).

## Fail-Fast Policy

**ONLY the exact allowed outputs listed per command are valid.** Anything else — gcloud auth errors, kubectl failures, tracebacks, empty output, unrecognized strings, timeouts — is an infrastructure failure. When it happens:

1. Do NOT guess or infer the result
2. Do NOT proceed with the operation
3. Report the exact command, full error output, and root cause to the caller
4. Leave any affected data untouched

---

## Commands

```bash
/Users/kenneth/Projects/ops/tsd/prod/run_django_mgmt_cmd.sh subscription_status '{email}'
```

**Allowed outputs (exact strings only):**
| Output | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| Exit 0, `"Free User"` | Free/trial user |
| Exit 0, `"Active Pro Subscriber"` | Paying subscriber |
| Exit 0, `"Expired Pro Subscriber"` | Lapsed subscriber — treat as free |
| Exit 1, `"No user found with email..."` | No account |

"""The credit ledger: lots of credits and what each charged turn took from them.

Balance is the sum of the lots still live, never a stored number, and a lot's
expiry is a comparison at read and charge time, so a lot simply stops counting.
"""
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import models


class CreditGrant(models.Model):
    """One lot of credits."""
    PACK = 'pack'
    SUBSCRIPTION = 'subscription'
    SIGNUP = 'signup'
    FREE = 'free'
    REWARD = 'reward'
    KINDS = [(k, k) for k in (PACK, SUBSCRIPTION, SIGNUP, FREE, REWARD)]

    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    kind = models.CharField(max_length=16, choices=KINDS)
    credits_granted = models.IntegerField()

    """One per charged turn. credits is 0 for a basic turn on a plan that includes
    them, and for a turn the app started."""
    BASIC = 'basic'
    EXPERT = 'expert'
    TIERS = [(BASIC, BASIC), (EXPERT, EXPERT)]
    PERSON = 'person'
    APP = 'app'
    ORIGINS = [(PERSON, PERSON), (APP, APP)]

    origin = models.CharField(max_length=8, choices=ORIGINS)

    class Meta:
        constraints = [models.UniqueConstraint(fields=['user', 'turn_id'], name='jusprin_credit_charge_once')]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=['user', 'created_at'])]

    credits = models.IntegerField()

# JusPrin 2.0.0 launch funnel — data collected, with sources

Written 2026-11-15 by session `local_3f0a1705-f0fd-409f-9ca9-21a4478aa21e`, for the session
working on where JusPrin 2 loses people between install and paying.

JusPrin 2.0.0 was tagged `jusprin/v2.0.0` and published 2026-11-13T03:24:19Z. Every count
below covers launch to roughly 2026-11-15 23:00 UTC unless the row says otherwise. Numbers I
measured are marked **measured**; numbers I calculated from other numbers are marked
**derived**; anything I did not verify is marked **unverified** and you should re-check it.

The per-account script is beside this file: `jusprin2-funnel-accounts.py`.

---

## 1. Funnel counts, per step

| Step | Count | Date range | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launch emails requested | 3,101 | 11-13 and 11-14 | **measured** — SendGrid `GET /v3/stats` daily, 770 + 2,331 |
| Delivered | 3,018 | same | **measured** — same call, 754 on 11-13 + 2,264 on 11-14 |
| Opened | ~697 | 11-13 → 11-15 | **measured** but day-summed, so a person who opened on two days counts twice |
| People who clicked | 33 | same | **measured** — `unique_clicks` 6 + 24 + 3 |
| Click events | 58 | same | **measured** — `clicks` 11 + 33 + 14 |
| Installer downloads | 96 | launch → 11-15 late | **measured** — GitHub release assets, excludes `SHA256SUMS.txt` |
| First launch of the app | **no data** | — | the desktop app ships no telemetry |
| Accounts created | 36 | 11-13 → 11-15 | **measured** — Django, syndicate `jusprinv2`, 37 total minus 1 pre-launch |
| Signed in and sent ≥1 message | 30 | same | **measured** — distinct `user` in `jusprin.CreditCharge` |
| Fixed or sliced a print | **no data** | — | `jusprin.PrintReport` and `PrintReportReview` are both 0 rows |
| Credits low / free month ending | **no data** | — | nothing records the moment a balance runs low |
| Opened checkout | **no data** | — | no server-side or product event for it that I could find |
| Paid | 1 | 11-15 | **measured** — Chargebee site `jusprinv2`, invoice #2, $10 |

Beware the funnel is not nested. 96 downloads is a count of **files**, not people, and most
repo visitors never saw the email (see section 5).

### Email, per batch

All three batches are legacy Marketing Campaigns on SendGrid. Batch 3 was a 2x2 test: two
subject lines by two sender display names, four campaigns.

| Batch | Sent | Delivered | Opened | Open rate | Clickers | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — free v1 users, last 30 days | 11-13 | 437 | 57 | 13.0% | 4 | **measured** — Email Activity, `from_email="jusprin-support@obico.io"` |
| 2 — free v1 users, last chat Sep 19–Oct 13 | 11-13 | 317 | 43 | 13.6% | 2 | **measured**, but see caveat below |
| 3, new subject "JusPrin 2 is here" | 11-14 18:00–21:00 | 1,127 | 324 | 28.7% | 11 | **measured** — Email Activity, `subject="JusPrin 2 is here"` |
| 3, old subject "JusPrin 2: open source AI slicer…" | same | 1,137 | ~273 | 24.0% | ~16 | **derived** — batch 3 category total minus the new-subject half |

Batch 2's row is windowed by `last_event_time` between 11-13T00:00Z and 11-14T17:00Z on
`from_email="support@obico.io"`, because batch 2 shares both its subject line and its from
address with batch 3a. Its segment held 204 recipients when created, so the 317 figure
probably includes some batch-1 tail. Treat it as approximate.

Batch 3 totals, **measured** from `GET /v3/categories/stats?categories=jusprin2-batch3`
(all four variants carry that one category): 2,331 requested, 2,264 delivered, 892 opens,
597 unique opens (day-summed), 46 click events, 27 unique clickers, 11 bounces, 36 blocks,
21 bounce drops, 4 invalid, 3 unsubscribes, 0 spam reports.

### What the clicks were

The email has three links: a YouTube video, `github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest`,
and `www.obico.io/blog/introducing-jusprin-2/`. None carry UTM parameters.

**Measured** for the new-subject half of batch 3, by fetching `GET /v3/messages/{msg_id}`
for each of its 11 clickers and reading the click events: 23 click events, 13 on the GitHub
release page and 10 on the blog post, none on the video. Distinct people: 10 clicked GitHub,
3 clicked the blog. Three of the 11 clickers have `opens_count` 0, which proves click
tracking does not depend on the open pixel.

---

## 2. Per-account breakdown

Run `jusprin2-funnel-accounts.py` in the production web pod to regenerate. As of
2026-11-15 23:00 UTC, over all 37 `jusprinv2` accounts:

| Group | Accounts |
|---|---|
| Signed in, never sent a message | 7 |
| Exactly one chat | 10 |
| Two or more chats | 20 |
| Came back on a later day | 6 |
| Bought credits or a plan | 2 (one of which is Kenneth's own test account) |
| Median turns among those who chatted | 10 |

Charges in total: 653 turns, 1,937 credits. By model alias, 631 turns and 1,915 credits on
`slicer-1` (Claude Sonnet, 5 credits a turn) against 22 turns and 22 credits on
`slicer-basic` (DeepSeek, 1 credit). Almost nobody uses the cheap model.

Signups and activity per day, **measured**:

| Day | Signups | People who sent a message | Turns charged |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11-13 | 11 | 7 | 145 |
| 11-14 | 9 | 12 | 278 |
| 11-15 | 16 | 17 | 215 |

Two accounts stand out and both need excluding from behavioural reads:

- `263741` is `k@obico.io`, Kenneth's own account. It holds the `jusprin-hobby-monthly`
  subscription created 2026-11-11T23:57, before launch, and Chargebee invoice #1 for $8.
  Any earlier claim that launch produced a paying subscriber was wrong; this is it.
- `264001` joined 11-13T02:16, an hour before the release was published, and has 32 chats
  and 144 turns over 4 days — far beyond every other account. **Unverified** who it is.

The one real customer, `264228`, matters for your question: it signed up at 11-15T09:11 and
bought a 1,000-credit pack at 11-15T09:19, **with zero chats and zero turns**. It did not
convert by using the product. The person replied to the launch email (Gmail message
`1a1de501d65f6160` in `k@obico.io`) saying he was buying "while the double credits last"
after contributing test prints during v1. So the one purchase so far is a supporter buying on
the announcement, not a user converting after hitting a limit.

---

## 3. Where each number came from

**Production database.** All queries through `kubectl --context=tsd exec` on a running
`tsdweb-prod` pod:

```bash
cd /Users/kenneth/Projects/ops/tsd/prod
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
pod=$(kubectl --context=tsd get pods -l app=tsdweb-prod \
      --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
kubectl --context=tsd cp script.py "$pod":/tmp/script.py
kubectl --context=tsd exec "$pod" -- python manage.py shell -c "exec(open('/tmp/script.py').read())"
```

Tables used, all in the `jusprin` app: `CreditGrant` (fields `user, kind, credits_granted,
credits_remaining, expires_at, source_ref, created_at`; kinds seen are `signup`,
`subscription`, `pack`), `CreditCharge` (`user, turn_id, chat_id, alias, tier, credits,
origin, created_at`), `CreditAllocation`, `ChatTitle` (`user, chat_id, title, updated_at`),
`PrintReport` and `PrintReportReview` (both empty). JusPrin 2 accounts are
`User.objects.filter(syndicate__name='jusprinv2')`. Obico v1 subscriptions live in a
different app, `app_ent.Subscription`.

Grant totals, **measured**: `signup` 38 grants / 19,000 granted / 17,063 remaining;
`subscription` 1 / 1,500 / 1,500; `pack` 1 / 1,000 / 1,000.

**Chargebee.** Two separate sites. JusPrin 2 is site `jusprinv2`, with its key in
`/Users/kenneth/Projects/ops/tsd/prod/tsdweb-prod.yaml` as `JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_API_KEY`;
Obico is site `thespaghettidetective` under `CHARGEBEE_API_KEY`. Use `curl -sg` — the `-g` is
needed or the shell globs `sort_by[desc]`.

```bash
curl -sg -u REDACTED "https://jusprinv2.chargebee.com/api/v2/invoices?limit=20&sort_by[desc]=date"
```

Only two invoices exist: #1 $8 on 11-11 to `jusprinv2-263741` (Kenneth), #2 $10 on
2026-11-15T09:18:55 to `jusprinv2-264228`. One active subscription, `AzylwXVaiDBan45t4`.

**SendGrid.** No API key needed if you drive it through an authenticated browser tab on
`mc.sendgrid.com` with `fetch(url, {credentials:'include'})`. Endpoints that worked:
`/v3/campaigns`, `/v3/campaigns/{id}` (includes `html_content`, `plain_content`,
`categories`, `segment_ids`, `sender_id`), `/v3/stats`, `/v3/categories/stats`,
`/v3/messages` (Email Activity), `/v3/messages/{msg_id}` (per-message event list with click
URLs), `/v3/marketing/senders`, `/v3/contactdb/segments/{id}`, `/v3/tracking_settings/*`.

---

## 4. Steps with no data at all

1. **First launch after install.** The desktop app sends nothing on startup. Of the 96
   downloads, roughly 60 never became an account and are completely invisible — we cannot
   tell an install that failed from one that was never opened.
2. **Downloads over time.** GitHub publishes only a running total per asset, no history. I
   have exactly two snapshots: 40 installer downloads at about 11-14 16:00 UTC, and 96 on
   11-15 late. If you want a curve, start sampling the release endpoint on a schedule now.
3. **Slicing and printing outcomes.** `PrintReport` and `PrintReportReview` have no rows, so
   "fixed or sliced a print" cannot be measured from the database. The GCS chat capture is
   the only route, and it needs reading chat by chat.
4. **Checkout opened, pricing page viewed.** I found no event for either.
5. **Credits running low.** Nothing records the moment a balance crosses a threshold. You can
   reconstruct it from `CreditGrant.credits_remaining` against `CreditCharge` history.
6. **PostHog.** I did not query it in the part of the session I can still see. No personal
   API key exists in the `ops` or `tsd-enterprise` repos — the only key in the website source
   (`www/src/js/analytics.js` on www.obico.io) is a `phc_` write key, which cannot read.
   Project ids 2971 "Obico" and 254544 "Whispr Notes" and the HogQL endpoint
   `/api/projects/{id}/query/` are **unverified** notes from earlier in the session. The
   desktop app does not send PostHog events at all, so PostHog can only ever cover the
   website, not the funnel steps you care about.
7. **Google Analytics.** Unread. Kenneth said "Skip GA" and declined to sign in.
8. **The sender half of the batch 3 A/B test.** Not recoverable. All four variants share the
   single SendGrid category `jusprin2-batch3`; both sender identities use the same
   `support@obico.io` address and differ only in display name, which Email Activity cannot
   filter on; the four segments (14025814–17) now report 0 recipients because membership
   drifted; and the legacy per-campaign stats page is down for maintenance.

---

## 5. What I concluded, and what I ruled out

**Downloads outrunning email clicks is not a tracking failure.** 96 counts files rather than
people, five files sit on the page one click lands on, 40 of the 96 were already taken before
batch 3 was even sent, and GitHub's own referrers say YouTube (69 uniques) and Google (68)
each bring more people to the repo over 14 days than the email does. On 11-14 the repo had 52
unique visitors against 24 unique email clickers, so the email is a real but minority source.

**One genuine undercount path for clicks, unmeasurable.** The email shows the bare URL
`https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest` as the visible, clickable
text, with the SendGrid tracker only in the `href`. Anyone who copies the visible URL, or
whose client or security gateway strips the anchor, reaches GitHub untracked. I cannot size
it: SendGrid's redirect passes no referrer, so `ct.sendgrid.net` appears nowhere in GitHub's
referrer list even though at least 13 clicks went through it, which means tracked and
untracked email arrivals look identical to GitHub. Batch 3's click-to-open ratio of 4.5% is
below the 10% or so a launch announcement usually gets, consistent with both an undercount
and a weak call to action.

**Ruled out: open tracking hiding clicks.** Three of 11 clickers registered zero opens, so
image-blocking clients still produce clicks.

**Ruled out: the subject line explaining batch 3's open rate.** Batch 3 opened at about 26%
against 13.0% and 13.6% for batches 1 and 2. The new subject beat the old one inside batch 3,
28.7% to 24.0%, which is real but much too small to explain the doubling. Batch 3a used the
same subject, the same from address and the same sender display name as batch 2 and went to a
**colder** audience (last chat on or before Sep 18), yet still roughly doubled it. Something
changed between 11-13 and 11-14, after the two GlockApps seed tests. I never established
what. Ask Kenneth.

**The gateway failures were a one-off window, and reporting is broken.** 29 upstream failures
**measured**, all status 400, format `anthropic`, alias `slicer-1`, all between 15:45 and
16:56 UTC on 11-14, and none since through 215 charged turns on 11-15. The cause is not
proven; the $30 monthly spend cap is the leading explanation. I disproved "the prompt was too
long" by running Anthropic's free `count_tokens` on the largest captured request (4.1 MB, 232
messages, 335,040 tokens against a 1M window). The real error text is unknown because
`_upstream_failed` in `web_ent/jusprin/v2/gateway.py` deliberately logs no response body.

Two structural facts behind that, both still unfixed and both relevant to your conversion
question because they silently cost users credits:

- `web_ent/jusprin/v2/gateway.py` reports to Sentry only when `is_gateway_fault(status)` is
  true, which `web_ent/jusprin/v2/upstream.py` defines as 401, 403 or 404. Status 400, 402
  and 429 never reach Sentry. The whole 11-14 outage was invisible.
- `admit()` in `web_ent/jusprin/v2/credits.py` charges credits **before** the upstream call,
  and there is no refund path anywhere in `web_ent/jusprin/ledger/`. Account `264021` lost
  credits to six consecutive failures and stopped at 15:47 on 11-14. It has 455 credits spent
  in total and has not returned since 11-15T01:07.

**JusPrin 1 users are never told 2.0.0 exists from inside the app.** At tag `jusprin/v1.4.0`,
`src/libslic3r/AppConfig.cpp:40` sets `VERSION_CHECK_URL` to
`https://check-version.orcaslicer.com/latest`. The commit that points the update check at
JusPrin's own releases, `80ed1692ff` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/UpdateCheck.cpp`), is
contained only in tag `jusprin/v2.0.0`. So email is the only channel to v1 users, which is
why the 13% open rate mattered. Consistent with this, the v1.4.0 release page is still the
most-viewed path on the repo, 189 unique visitors against 59 for v2.0.0.

**Retention, not acquisition, is where this is leaking.** Only 6 of 37 accounts came back on
a later day, and the median chatter spends 10 turns. The one purchase came from a supporter
with zero chats. Nothing in the data yet shows a person hitting a limit and buying.

---

## 6. What Kenneth has said or decided

- "Skip GA" — he declined to sign into Google Analytics, so GA4 stays unread.
- He wants findings as visuals, not prose. I delivered the funnel, the per-batch open rates,
  the daily curves and the referrer breakdown as charts.
- He has **not** decided between fixing the Sentry blind spot plus credit refunds, and
  investigating email deliverability first. I asked; it is still open.
- He has **not** decided whether to reword the email links and add UTM parameters before the
  remaining send. I asked at the end of my last turn; also open.
- Still unemailed: roughly 20 paying JusPrin 1 subscribers. That count came from earlier in
  my session and I have **not** re-verified it. Every free v1 user is now covered by the
  three batches.
- He has made no decision at all about what to build to improve conversion. That is your
  question, and nothing in my session pre-empts it.

Two things worth telling him plainly, because I only found them late: the $8 subscription
counted as the first sale is his own account, and the one real customer bought without
chatting even once.

U  = get_user_model()

rows = []

"""Per-turn admission: rate limit, then the turn's charge in the credit ledger.

A turn is everything the client sends for one reply, including tool-call
follow-ups; every request of it carries the same X-JusPrin-Turn value. A turn
pays its model's price once, however many requests it makes. Title requests are
free, and a request of kind "note" is a turn the app started, not the person.

The reply requests of one turn are sequential (a follow-up is built from the
previous answer), so the charge does not guard against two reply requests of
the same turn racing each other.
"""
import enum
import time

from django.conf import settings

from jusprin.ledger.ledger import charge_turn
from jusprin.ledger.models import CreditCharge
from lib.cache import REDIS

KEY_PREFIX = 'jusprin:v2'
TURN_TTL_SECONDS = 60 * 60


class Admission(enum.Enum):
    ADMITTED = 'admitted'
    RATE_LIMITED = 'rate_limited'


def admit(user_id: int, turn_id: str, request_kind: str, alias, chat_id: str = None) -> Admission:
    """Count a new turn against the rate limit, then charge it once unless it
    is a title. Raises ledger.CreditsExhausted when it cannot be paid.
    Synchronous: Redis and the credit tables are both blocking."""
    seen_key = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:seen:{user_id}:{turn_id}'
    if REDIS.set(seen_key, '1', nx=True, ex=TURN_TTL_SECONDS):
        bucket = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:turns:{user_id}:{int(time.time() // 60)}'
        pipe = REDIS.pipeline()
        pipe.incr(bucket)
        pipe.expire(bucket, 120)
        turns_this_minute, _ = pipe.execute()
        if turns_this_minute > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_TURNS_PER_MINUTE:
            # The turn was not admitted, so its retry is a new turn again.
            REDIS.delete(seen_key)
            return Admission.RATE_LIMITED

    if request_kind == 'title':
        return Admission.ADMITTED

    charged_key = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:charged:{user_id}:{turn_id}'
    if not REDIS.set(charged_key, '1', nx=True, ex=TURN_TTL_SECONDS):
        return Admission.ADMITTED
    origin = CreditCharge.APP if request_kind == 'note' else CreditCharge.PERSON
    charged = False
    try:
        charge_turn(user_id, turn_id, alias, origin, chat_id)
        charged = True
    finally:
        # Only a turn that actually paid is remembered as paid, whether the
        # credits ran out or the credit tables raised.
        if not charged:
            REDIS.delete(charged_key)
    return Admission.ADMITTED

The counts come from the "Jusprin 2.0.0 conversion and traction analysis" session's collection (notes folder, `jusprin2-funnel-data.md`), re-run by me tonight, plus a read of all 110 kept chats in the `prod-jusprin-v2` bucket, which that session had not done. Re-run recipe: notes folder, `jusprin2-funnel-rerun.md`.

## The funnel

| Step | People | Notes | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launch emails delivered | 3,018 | 11-13 and 11-14, three batches | SendGrid `/v3/stats` (sibling session) |
| Clicked a link in the email | 33 | most clicks went to the GitHub release page | SendGrid Email Activity (sibling session) |
| Installer downloads | 96 | files, not people; YouTube and Google bring more repo visitors than the email | GitHub release assets API, snapshot 11-16 02:55 UTC |
| First launch | no data | the app sends nothing on start; its update check calls api.github.com, which we cannot read | `Updates/UpdateCheck.cpp` |
| Signed in (account created) | 36 | plus Kenneth's own pre-launch account, excluded below. Sign-in is optional, so some of the other 60 downloads may be slicing without an account | Django, `User` in syndicate `jusprinv2` |
| Sent at least one message to the AI | 26 | 7 signed in and never chatted; 3 more opened a file, got the file report, and sent nothing | `CreditCharge` rows; kept chats, user text blocks |
| Loaded a file into a chat | 22 | | kept chats, file-load reports |
| Sliced successfully at least once | 16 | | kept chats, `slice_report` results with a print time |
| Exported G-code or opened the print dialog | 9 | | kept chats, `export_file` / `print_dialog_open` succeeded |
| Came back on a day after sign-up | 5 of 20 | only accounts from 11-13 and 11-14 have had the chance | `CreditCharge.created_at` vs `date_joined` |
| Credits running low | 1 | nobody is at zero; median spend is 20 of 500; one account has 45 left | `CreditGrant.credits_remaining` |
| Opened the pricing page from the app | 3 | the buyer; one person after a 6-minute chat; the 45-credits person, who did not buy | load-balancer logs, `POST /ent/jusprin/v2/web_link` |
| Paid | 1 | a $10 pack, bought 8 minutes after sign-in with zero chats | Chargebee site `jusprinv2`, invoice #2 (sibling session) |

Per-account activity is in the scratch TSV and the re-run recipe; per-chat results in `chats.json` beside it.

## Where people drop

The one measurable big drop is between signing in and finishing a slice: 36 people sign in, 16 slice. Of the 20 who don't, 7 never send anything, 3 leave right after the file report, and 10 chat but never slice; 5 of those 10 spent their chats setting up a printer and then stopped. My hypothesis is that printer setup is where several stall, but ten people is too few to say.

The step Kenneth's question is about, running low on credits, has nobody in it yet. The out-of-credits card has never been shown to anyone. The "About 25 credits left" notice has never fired either. The free month ends 12-13 at the earliest. So neither a drip email nor a pop-up at that moment can be judged from this data for another few weeks.

The one purchase was not a conversion. The buyer looked at the pricing page in a browser three times between 08:33 and 08:59 on 11-15, signed in at 09:16, pressed Get more credits at 09:16, and bought at 09:18. He is a JusPrin 1 tester who replied to the launch email saying he was buying while double credits last.

The one person near the limit got there partly through a bug. Account 264021 lost 30 credits to six upstream 400s on 11-14 (credits are charged before the model call and never refunded), stopped, signed in again on 11-15 at 12:00, opened the pricing page, and left. The sibling session found this; it is still unfixed.

Return rate is consistent with Kenneth's "sign in and stop opening the app" hypothesis: 5 of the 20 eligible accounts came back. But three days is too short to call it. Check at day 7 and day 14.

## What I recommend first

1. Fix the credit charge on a failed model call and the Sentry blind spot for 400/402/429. It is the only observed path to the purchase moment and it is broken. Measure: upstream failures in Cloud Logging against `CreditCharge` rows with no reply.
2. Two log lines on the server, no app change: the user id on each `web_link` open with its `from` field, and the user id on each `/account` call. The first gives "opened pricing, from where, who" per person. The second gives daily active signed-in users, so return can be measured without a chat. Both are the person's own account data, no consent change.
3. Re-run the counts on 11-20 and 11-27 before building anything for the credit moment. At about 12 sign-ups a day, a before/after read on "came back within 7 days" needs about 150 accounts per arm to see a rise from 25% to 40%, so roughly four weeks of sign-ups for a holdout test. Anything built sooner cannot be measured.

## What I rule out for now

A scheduled drip and a generic upgrade pop-up, for the reason Kenneth already had: no step shows people stalling on a calendar. A lifecycle email to people who signed in and never chatted is allowed under the policy and is the most plausible first email, but with 7 such people there is nothing to measure yet; write it, send it by hand once the group is about 30, and compare their 7-day return with the people who were not emailed.

## Still unknown

How many of the 96 downloads became a first launch, and how many people use the app without signing in. Who account 264001 is: it joined an hour before the release was published and has 32 chats, far above everyone else, and it is not on a team email domain. Whether the return rate holds once the 11-15 cohort has had a week.

## Decision needed

Decision needed: do you want an anonymous first-launch ping from the app to our server? Today the app's update check goes to GitHub's API, which gives us nothing. A ping with the version, platform and a random install id would make the download-to-launch step measurable and would also count people who slice without signing in. It costs an app release and a sentence in the privacy policy, since a random install id is arguably personal data. The alternative is to accept that step as unmeasurable and judge acquisition by sign-ups alone. My pick is the ping, in the next release, with the id reset on reinstall. Which do you want?
